titleStmt.title: Time cells in the hippocampus: a new dimension for mapping memories
titleStmt.author: Eichenbaum

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Time cells in the hippocampus: a new dimension for mapping memories

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: whether hippocampal neurons code elapsed time as a dimension in its own right, and how that coding relates to spatial coding
span.quote: Recent studies have revealed the existence of hippocampal neurons that fire at successive moments in temporally structured experiences. Several studies have shown that such temporal coding is not attributable to external events, specific behaviours or spatial dimensions of an experience. Instead, these cells represent the flow of time in specific memories and have therefore been dubbed

span.label: the firing properties of time cells parallel those of place cells point for point, so time is an additional dimension integrated with spatial mapping rather than a separate system
span.quote: The firing properties of time cells parallel those of hippocampal place cells; time cells thus provide an additional dimension that is integrated with spatial mapping.

span.label: existence
span.quote: Recent studies have revealed the existence of hippocampal neurons that fire at successive moments in temporally structured experiences.

span.label: hippocampal time cells
span.quote: Instead, these cells represent the flow of time in specific memories and have therefore been dubbed ‘time cells’.

span.label: review
span.quote: Here I evaluate this hypothesis, discussing first the evidence for the existence of hippocampal time cells, their characteristics and their role in memory.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Slowly evolving cortical temporal-context signals select among preconfigured intra-hippocampal firing chains, so that a given chain comes to represent a particular temporally organised memory
span.quote: Combining the findings that support the existence of firing chains with the observations that a broader signal that defines entire memories is needed, perhaps the most likely network mechanism involves slowly evolving temporal context dynamics (that is, signals that spread across multiple sequential events) selecting specific firing chains that represent specific temporally organized memories

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Cortical areas of the 'where' stream deliver temporal-context signals to the hippocampus, which then parses that continuous context into discrete time fields
span.quote: Combined, these findings suggest that signals about the temporal context of experience are sent via a network of cortical areas to the hippocampus, which then parses temporal context into discrete units (time fields) that represent the flow of sequential events

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Repeated sequential activation strengthens connections so each place cell is driven by an earlier-firing cell, producing the backward expansion of place fields
span.quote: This backward expansion of place fields could reflect each place cell being driven by an earlier-firing place cell through enhanced connectivity that is generated by repeated sequential activation.

span.label: temporal information generated in the cerebral cortex and other brain areas may provide signals to time cells, or the phenomenon may arise from firing chains generated locally within the hippocampal circuitry
span.quote: It is possible that temporal information generated in the cerebral cortex and other brain areas provides signals to time cells within the hippocampus ( FIG. 6a ). Alternatively, the time-cell phenomenon might arise from the sequential activation of firing chains that are generated locally within the hippocampal circuitry

span.label: the chaining account is supported by place fields expanding backwards from their centre with repeated runs, as if each cell were driven by an earlier-firing one
span.quote: This model is consistent with the finding that when rats repeatedly run through a sequence of locations, the place fields of hippocampal neurons expand backwards from their original centre

span.label: the proposed resolution is a slowly evolving temporal context selecting among preconfigured firing chains, rather than either alone
span.quote: Combining the findings that support the existence of firing chains with the observations that a broader signal that defines entire memories is needed, perhaps the most likely network mechanism involves slowly evolving temporal context dynamics (that is, signals that spread across multiple sequential events) selecting specific firing chains that represent specific temporally organized memories

span.label: prefrontal and parietal areas of the where stream turn out to be involved in the perception of time and project strongly to the hippocampus
span.quote: These findings suggest that prefrontal areas and parietal areas that are classically considered part of the ‘where’ stream (that is, the visual stream for spatial processing) are also involved in the perception of time, and these areas have robust inputs to the hippocampus.

span.label: The origin of hippocampal timing signals - external input versus internally generated firing chains - is left unresolved.
span.note: what this limits: any mechanistic reading of time cells: IT REMAINS A CENTRAL QUESTION WHETHER TEMPORAL INFORMATION ... ORIGINATES FROM ITS INPUTS OR IS GENERATED INTERNALLY
span.quote: It remains a central question whether temporal information represented within the hippocampus originates from its inputs or is generated internally, or whether a combination of mechanisms generates time cells.

span.label: The evidence reviewed is almost entirely restricted to hippocampal area CA1.
span.note: what this limits: the anatomical reach of the whole review: STUDIES OF TIME CELLS HAVE FOCUSED ON HIPPOCAMPAL AREA CA1 BECAUSE THIS AREA SEEMS TO BE THE MOST IMPORTANT FOR TEMPORAL ORGANIZATION
span.quote: It is important to note that studies of time cells have focused on hippocampal area CA1 because this area seems to be the most important for temporal organization 73 .

span.label: The temporal/spatial distinction may be superficial if both reduce to association by proximity.
span.note: what this limits: the time/space distinction the review is built on: IT REMAINS ENTIRELY POSSIBLE THAT THE COMMON THREAD IN BOTH DIMENSIONS IS 'ASSOCIATION BY PROXIMITY' IN SPACE OR TIME
span.quote: Finally, although both spatial and temporal coding are prevalent in the activity patterns of hippocampal neurons, and can be distinguished experimentally, it remains entirely possible that the common thread in both dimensions is ‘association by proximity’ in space or time.

span.label: whether the temporal signal comes from the inputs, is generated internally, or both, is left as the central open question
span.note: duplicate of: limitations[0] · what this limits: the same scope as item 0 - inputs, internal generation, or a combination, all still open
span.quote: It remains a central question whether temporal information represented within the hippocampus originates from its inputs or is generated internally, or whether a combination of mechanisms generates time cells.

span.label: one study reports new temporal patterns emerging with learning rather than existing chains being co-opted, against the preconfigured account
span.note: what this limits: the co-opted-chains account specifically: one study REPORTED THE EMERGENCE OF NEW TEMPORAL PATTERNS OF NEURONAL FIRINGS ASSOCIATED WITH LEARNING, RATHER THAN A CO-OPTING OF EXISTING FIRING CHAINS
span.quote: However, one study examining trace eye-blink conditioning reported the emergence of new temporal patterns of neuronal firings associated with learning, rather than a co-opting of existing firing chains

span.label: the human recordings show slowly changing patterns rather than the punctate time-cell activations seen in rodents, so the cross-species claim rests on a phenomenon of different form
span.note: what this limits: the human-to-rodent join: the human patterns MORE CLOSELY RESEMBLE THE GRADUALLY EVOLVING TIME SIGNAL ... THAN THE SEQUENCES OF PUNCTATE TIME-CELL ACTIVATIONS in rodents, and are still read as the same phenomenon
span.quote: Although these slowly changing activity patterns more closely resemble the gradually evolving time signal in the study by Manns et al. 12 than the sequences of punctate time-cell activations in the above-described studies on rodents, these observations clearly demonstrate that temporal coding by neuronal activity related to memory also occurs in the human hippocampus.

span.label: studies of time cells have focused on hippocampal area CA1, with some evidence for CA2 but not CA3
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 1, with what is known outside CA1: THERE IS SOME EVIDENCE THAT AREA CA2 (BUT NOT CA3) COULD ALSO BE IMPORTANT FOR TEMPORAL PROCESSING
span.quote: It is important to note that studies of time cells have focused on hippocampal area CA1 because this area seems to be the most important for temporal organization 73 . However, there is some evidence that area CA2 (but not CA3) could also be important for temporal processing, suggesting that time cells might originate within the hippocampal circuitry

span.label: the author's closing possibility is that time cells and place cells are both reflections of association by proximity, which would dissolve the distinction the review is built on
span.note: what this limits: the same scope as item 2, with the consequence spelled out: PLACE CELLS AND TIME CELLS ARE SIMPLY REFLECTIONS OF A BASIC FUNCTION OF THE HIPPOCAMPUS
span.quote: Finally, although both spatial and temporal coding are prevalent in the activity patterns of hippocampal neurons, and can be distinguished experimentally, it remains entirely possible that the common thread in both dimensions is ‘association by proximity’ in space or time. This would suggest that place cells and time cells are simply reflections of a basic function of the hippocampus — supporting associative networks that represent a broad range of relations among the elements of memories

span.label: the cue-and-structure vocabulary carried over term by term: temporal cues answering to spatial cues, temporal structure to spatial structure
span.quote: Time cells are controlled by the temporal cues (the beginning and end of an episode) and the temporal structure (critical intervals) of an experience, just as place cells are controlled by the spatial cues (landmarks) and the spatial structure (shape) of the environment.

span.label: scalar timing, imported as the criterion a neural code must satisfy to count as a code for time
span.quote: Importantly, the authors 18 observed that cells firing later in the delay period were active for longer durations (that is, they had larger ‘time-fields’) ( FIG. 1 ), a phenomenon that was also observed in other studies 19 , 20 (discussed below). This pattern suggests a scalar coding of time, which parallels a hallmark property of time judgements in humans and animals, as discussed below.

span.label: time cell and place cell are two names for ONE population - the same neurons, distinguished by which dimension the experiment lets you measure, not by which cells they are
span.quote: Time cells are the same neurons as place cells. One line of evidence supporting this conclusion is that, in freely moving animals, time cells are activated only when the animal is in a particular location

span.label: the parallel is term for term, not loose analogy: temporal cues answer to spatial cues, temporal structure to spatial structure, re-timing to re-mapping, time fields to place fields
span.quote: Time cells are controlled by the temporal cues (the beginning and end of an episode) and the temporal structure (critical intervals) of an experience, just as place cells are controlled by the spatial cues (landmarks) and the spatial structure (shape) of the environment.

span.label: the name 'time cell' is a coinage of one particular study, made on the strength of an analogy to place cells - because they fire at moments as place cells fire at locations - rather than on a mechanism
span.quote: Because these neurons fired at specific moments in a fixed period — much like place cells fire at specific locations in a fixed space — these neurons were dubbed

span.label: scalar coding - later cells firing for longer - is not decoration but the property that adjudicates between the two mechanisms, since uniform-duration chains cannot produce it
span.quote: In addition, firing sequences of time cells are usually scalar, so that time cells that fire later in a sequence also fire for a longer period ( FIGS 1b , 2B ; but see REF. 16 ). This is inconsistent with firing chains involving uniform-duration neuronal activations but is consistent with a recent variation on the temporal context model known as the scalar temporal context model

span.label: temporal coding in humans means gradually changing population patterns, while in rodents it means punctate successive activations; the review says so while treating both as the same finding
span.quote: Although these slowly changing activity patterns more closely resemble the gradually evolving time signal in the study by Manns et al. 12 than the sequences of punctate time-cell activations in the above-described studies on rodents, these observations clearly demonstrate that temporal coding by neuronal activity related to memory also occurs in the human hippocampus.

span.label: judging an interval and remembering temporal organisation are separated, with the hippocampus central only to the second - so 'timing' names two roles with different anatomy
span.quote: This view is consistent with a recently proposed distinction between the ability to judge temporal intervals, in which the hippocampus has a secondary role, and memory for temporal organization, in which the hippocampus is central

span.label: claim_type: existence
span.note: a second reading reaching the same value. Recorded: existence — a second reading reaching the same value from a different sentence. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: Recent studies have revealed the existence of hippocampal neurons that fire at successive moments in temporally structured experiences. Several studies have shown that such temporal coding is not attributable to external events, specific behaviours or spatial dimensions of an experience. Instead, these cells represent the flow of time in specific memories and have therefore been dubbed

span.label: phenomenon: hippocampal neurons firing at successive specific moments within a temporally structured period, filling it out
span.note: a second reading DIFFERING from the recorded value. Recorded: hippocampal time cells — a second reading, verbatim-verified, disagreeing with the value on the record. Not applied - a person decides.
span.quote: recent evidence shows that there are also hippocampal ‘time cells’ that fire when an animal is at a particular moment in a temporally structured experience, encoding scalar time and controlled by temporal dimensions of the experience

span.label: contradicts → the view that the fundamental function of the hippocampus is spatial mapping and navigation (the paper's reference 75)
span.quote: This challenges the view that the fundamental function of the hippocampus is spatial mapping and navigation 75 , and instead supports the notion that the hippocampus contributes to memory by organizing elements of experience in both spatial and temporal context.

span.label: builds-on → the scalar temporal context model (the paper's reference 69)
span.quote: This is inconsistent with firing chains involving uniform-duration neuronal activations but is consistent with a recent variation on the temporal context model known as the scalar temporal context model 69 .

span.label: contradicts → the view that the fundamental function of the hippocampus is spatial mapping and navigation
span.quote: This challenges the view that the fundamental function of the hippocampus is spatial mapping and navigation 75 , and instead supports the notion that the hippocampus contributes to memory by organizing elements of experience in both spatial and temporal context.

span.label: critiques → the strict chaining model in which time cells are a single fixed sequence of cell activations
span.quote: Several findings suggest that a strict chaining model, composed of a single sequence of cell activations, is unlikely to be the mechanism for time cells.

span.label: builds-on → the temporal context model of hippocampal coding, in its scalar variant
span.quote: In addition, firing sequences of time cells are usually scalar, so that time cells that fire later in a sequence also fire for a longer period ( FIGS 1b , 2B ; but see REF. 16 ). This is inconsistent with firing chains involving uniform-duration neuronal activations but is consistent with a recent variation on the temporal context model known as the scalar temporal context model

span.label: qualifies → the original reports of hippocampal temporal coding, criticised as confounded by location and distance travelled
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS A SPATIAL CONFOUND. The original temporal-coding reports 'were initially CRITICIZED AS BEING CONFOUNDED BY EFFECTS OF VARIATIONS IN THE ANIMAL'S LOCATION ACROSS TIME and of distance travelled over time, so that THE APPARENT TEMPORAL CODING COULD REFLECT SPATIAL rathe[r than temporal] coding'. The finding is not denied - an alternative explanation for it is offered, on one named variable. Q-443.
span.quote: These findings generated considerable interest but were initially criticized as being confounded by effects of variations in the animal's location across time and of distance travelled over time, so that the apparent temporal coding could reflect spatial rather than temporal dimensions of the animal's experience

span.label: extends → the place-cell account of hippocampal function, by adding a temporal dimension carried by the same cells
span.quote: The firing properties of time cells parallel those of hippocampal place cells; time cells thus provide an additional dimension that is integrated with spatial mapping.

span.label: time cells —same-as→ place cells
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — THE STRONGEST SAME-AS IN THE CORPUS: not two populations but one, given two names by two literatures. No lexical join could find this
span.quote: Time cells are the same neurons as place cells. One line of evidence supporting this conclusion is that, in freely moving animals, time cells are activated only when the animal is in a particular location

span.label: time cells —contrasted-with→ place cells
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.6 — the record marks this weak — and yet they are systematically OPPOSED term by term - temporal cues against spatial cues, temporal structure against spatial structure. Same cells, mirrored vocabularies
span.quote: Time cells are controlled by the temporal cues (the beginning and end of an episode) and the temporal structure (critical intervals) of an experience, just as place cells are controlled by the spatial cues (landmarks) and the spatial structure (shape) of the environment.

span.label: re-time —same-as→ re-map
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — one process under two names, and the review states the parallel explicitly rather than leaving it to be noticed
span.quote: For example, when a salient spatial cue in a familiar environment is altered, place cells either continue firing in association with the remaining spatial cues or ‘re-map’ (that is, alter the spatial firing pattern, or cease or begin firing) 27 . Similarly, when the duration of the interval between cues in an object–odour association task is altered, some time cells maintain firing at a specific time relative to the beginning or end of the interval, whereas many other cells ‘re-time’ — that is, fire at a different moment, or cease or begin firing

span.label: scalar coding —operationalised-as→ time-fields
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — scalar time is read off the width of the field, not off any clock
span.quote: Importantly, the authors 18 observed that cells firing later in the delay period were active for longer durations (that is, they had larger ‘time-fields’) ( FIG. 1 ), a phenomenon that was also observed in other studies 19 , 20 (discussed below). This pattern suggests a scalar coding of time, which parallels a hallmark property of time judgements in humans and animals, as discussed below.

span.label: firing chains —contrasted-with→ temporal context
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — CRITERION: uniform-duration chains cannot produce later cells that fire longer, and scalar firing is what the temporal context model predicts
span.quote: In addition, firing sequences of time cells are usually scalar, so that time cells that fire later in a sequence also fire for a longer period ( FIGS 1b , 2B ; but see REF. 16 ). This is inconsistent with firing chains involving uniform-duration neuronal activations but is consistent with a recent variation on the temporal context model known as the scalar temporal context model

span.label: temporal context —contrasted-with→ chaining model
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — external source against internal generation - the two candidate origins the review is organised around
span.quote: In the temporal context model, each hippocampal neuron represents a unique state of cortical activity that corresponds to moments in the stream of events processed within the cortex 69 . b | According to the chaining model, hippocampal neurons increase sequential connection strengths with repeated experiences to produce hippocampal neuron firing sequences

span.label: temporal context —causes→ firing chains
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — the proposed resolution: context SELECTS among chains rather than either mechanism acting alone. A proposal, hedged as 'perhaps the most likely' - weighted accordingly
span.quote: Combining the findings that support the existence of firing chains with the observations that a broader signal that defines entire memories is needed, perhaps the most likely network mechanism involves slowly evolving temporal context dynamics (that is, signals that spread across multiple sequential events) selecting specific firing chains that represent specific temporally organized memories

span.label: elapsed time —distinct-from→ distance travelled
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — DECOUPLED BY DESIGN: treadmill speed varied randomly per trial so the two could be separated at all
span.quote: The authors varied the treadmill speed randomly on each trial, so that the effects of elapsed time and distance travelled on neural activity could be disentangled.

span.label: distance travelled —contrasted-with→ elapsed time
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — AND THE CONFOUND SURVIVED: most cells encoded BOTH, to differing degrees - decoupling vindicated the variable without eliminating the rival
span.quote: A general linear model analysis that considered head position, time and distance revealed that the activity of over 80% of the neurons that were active during treadmill running was modulated by elapsed time. Position had little influence, but distance travelled was also strongly encoded in the activity of many neurons. The firing patterns of some neurons signalled only time or only distance, but the activity of most cells was influenced to differing degrees by both variables, indicating that most of these cells encoded both time and distance.

span.label: treadmill —operationalised-as→ elapsed time
span.note: strength of the relation: 1
span.quote: The authors varied the treadmill speed randomly on each trial, so that the effects of elapsed time and distance travelled on neural activity could be disentangled.

span.label: general linear model —operationalised-as→ elapsed time
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — time is what is left after head position and distance are taken out - a residual, not a direct measurement
span.quote: A general linear model analysis that considered head position, time and distance revealed that the activity of over 80% of the neurons that were active during treadmill running was modulated by elapsed time. Position had little influence, but distance travelled was also strongly encoded in the activity of many neurons. The firing patterns of some neurons signalled only time or only distance, but the activity of most cells was influenced to differing degrees by both variables, indicating that most of these cells encoded both time and distance.

span.label: head-fixed —operationalised-as→ time cells
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — the last rung of the ladder - remove location and movement entirely rather than model them
span.quote: Further evidence supporting the existence of temporal signals that are independent of place or distance has come from recent studies of time cells in head-fixed animals in which the animal's location and behaviour were kept constant and movement was eliminated.

span.label: grid cells —part-of→ entorhinal cortex
span.note: strength of the relation: 1 — and they too fire at particular moments, so the same dual coding appears one synapse upstream
span.quote: there is recent evidence that medial entorhinal cortex neurons that fire when a rat is in particular locations in space (known as ‘grid cells’) also fire at particular moments during treadmill running

span.label: CA1 —contrasted-with→ CA2
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.7 — SCOPE: nearly all the evidence is CA1; CA2 has some support and CA3 explicitly none
span.quote: It is important to note that studies of time cells have focused on hippocampal area CA1 because this area seems to be the most important for temporal organization 73 . However, there is some evidence that area CA2 (but not CA3) could also be important for temporal processing, suggesting that time cells might originate within the hippocampal circuitry

span.label: parietal areas —causes→ hippocampus
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.8 — areas classed with the spatial stream turn out to be involved in the perception of time, and they project strongly here - the stream's NAME is itself the problem. The quote says 'suggest', so this is an inference about routing, not a demonstrated path
span.quote: These findings suggest that prefrontal areas and parietal areas that are classically considered part of the ‘where’ stream (that is, the visual stream for spatial processing) are also involved in the perception of time, and these areas have robust inputs to the hippocampus.

span.label: association by proximity —distinct-from→ time cells
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.6 — the record marks this weak — THE AUTHOR'S OWN DEFLATION: if the common thread is proximity, then time cells and place cells are both epiphenomena of one associative function
span.quote: Finally, although both spatial and temporal coding are prevalent in the activity patterns of hippocampal neurons, and can be distinguished experimentally, it remains entirely possible that the common thread in both dimensions is ‘association by proximity’ in space or time. This would suggest that place cells and time cells are simply reflections of a basic function of the hippocampus — supporting associative networks that represent a broad range of relations among the elements of memories

span.label: trace eye-blink conditioning —distinct-from→ firing chains
span.note: differs in: THE AXIS IS WHETHER LEARNING CREATES THE PATTERN OR RECRUITS ONE. 'one study examining trace eye-blink conditioning REPORTED THE EMERGENCE OF NEW TEMPORAL PATTERNS of neuronal firings associated with learning, RATHER THAN A CO-OPTING OF EXISTING FIRING CHAINS.' Both accounts predict temporally structured firing after learning and differ only on where the structure came from - which is invisible in the trained animal and visible only across learning. Q-466. · strength of the relation: 0.8 — the dissenting paradigm: new patterns EMERGED with learning rather than existing chains being co-opted
span.quote: However, one study examining trace eye-blink conditioning reported the emergence of new temporal patterns of neuronal firings associated with learning, rather than a co-opting of existing firing chains

span.label: Hippocampal CA1 principal cells encode the temporal structure of remembered experience independently of the animal's location and movement.
span.quote: Together, these observations provide compelling evidence that the principal cells of hippocampal area CA1 encode the temporal structure of events in remembered experiences independently of any effects of location and movement on neuronal activity.

span.label: Time cells and place cells are not distinct populations — the same hippocampal neurons carry both codes.
span.quote: Finally, time cells and place cells are the same neurons, and the same neuronal ensembles can encode the temporal and spatial organization of experiences.

span.label: Time-cell firing sequences emerge with learning, are specific to particular memories, and predict whether a subsequent memory judgement will be correct.
span.quote: Also, there is now compelling evidence that firing sequences of time cells develop with learning, are memory specific and predict the accuracy of subsequent memory across a broad variety of tasks.

span.label: A strict chaining account of time cells is rejected, chiefly because elongating a delay makes cells re-time rather than simply lengthening a chain, and because chains cannot split to disambiguate overlapping memories.
span.quote: Several findings suggest that a strict chaining model, composed of a single sequence of cell activations, is unlikely to be the mechanism for time cells.

span.label: The prevalence of temporal coding argues against a purely spatial-navigation account of hippocampal function in favour of organising experience in both space and time.
span.quote: This challenges the view that the fundamental function of the hippocampus is spatial mapping and navigation

span.label: the original temporal-coding reports were criticised as confounded by the animal's changing location and by distance travelled over time
span.quote: These findings generated considerable interest but were initially criticized as being confounded by effects of variations in the animal's location across time and of distance travelled over time, so that the apparent temporal coding could reflect spatial rather than temporal dimensions of the animal's experience

span.label: later studies addressed this by tightly controlling the animal's location and movement
span.quote: More recent studies have addressed these concerns by tightly controlling the animal's location and movement.

span.label: FIRST RUNG: cells with reliable place fields were simply excluded from the analysis
span.quote: The rats could move freely during the delay, but cells that had reliable place fields were excluded from the analysis, indicating that the measured activity patterns encoded time rather than place.

span.label: SECOND RUNG: a general linear model separated location, speed and head direction from elapsed time, leaving an independent contribution of time
span.quote: Extensive general linear model analysis was used to distinguish activity patterns associated with the animal's location, speed and head direction during the delay period from activity patterns associated with the time elapsed. Although these spatial and behavioural parameters contributed to the activity patterns of many of the recorded cells, the analysis also revealed a contribution of time that was independent of these variables.

span.label: THIRD RUNG, THE DECOUPLING: treadmill speed was randomised per trial so that elapsed time and distance travelled could be disentangled
span.quote: The authors varied the treadmill speed randomly on each trial, so that the effects of elapsed time and distance travelled on neural activity could be disentangled.

span.label: over 80 percent of active neurons were modulated by elapsed time, position mattered little, but distance was also strongly encoded and most cells carried both
span.quote: A general linear model analysis that considered head position, time and distance revealed that the activity of over 80% of the neurons that were active during treadmill running was modulated by elapsed time. Position had little influence, but distance travelled was also strongly encoded in the activity of many neurons. The firing patterns of some neurons signalled only time or only distance, but the activity of most cells was influenced to differing degrees by both variables, indicating that most of these cells encoded both time and distance.

span.label: FOURTH RUNG: head-fixed preparations removed location and movement altogether
span.quote: Further evidence supporting the existence of temporal signals that are independent of place or distance has come from recent studies of time cells in head-fixed animals in which the animal's location and behaviour were kept constant and movement was eliminated.

span.label: the conclusion the ladder licenses: CA1 principal cells encode temporal structure independently of location and movement
span.quote: Together, these observations provide compelling evidence that the principal cells of hippocampal area CA1 encode the temporal structure of events in remembered experiences independently of any effects of location and movement on neuronal activity.

span.label: AN EARLY DISSOCIATION: spatial representations differed across trials too, but equally on correct and error trials, so they did not predict memory accuracy
span.quote: The firing patterns of the same hippocampal ensemble also varied with the locations at which the odours were presented, but the differences in spatial representations were equivalent in correct trials and error trials, and therefore did not predict the accuracy of the memory performance.

span.label: the firing patterns of many neurons re-timed when the delay was increased, even though the behaviour and locations of the animal during the initial period did not change
span.quote: Furthermore, the firing patterns of many of these neurons changed (that is, they ‘re-timed’) when the delay was increased. This happened even though the behaviour and locations of the animal during the initial period did not change ( FIG. 3A ; also see FIG. 1b ), indicating that the firing patterns of these cells reflected the passage of time rather than variations in behaviour or place.

span.label: cells firing later in the delay were active for longer, a scalar coding of time paralleling human and animal time judgements
span.note: WHOSE RESULT THIS IS: the authors 18 observed - THE EVIDENCE FOR THIS ROW ATTRIBUTES THE WORK TO SOMEBODY ELSE. The cited name is the subject of a result verb and the sentence carries no first-person marker, so the finding, quantity or definition is the CITED author's rather than this record's. The claim is true and the quote is verbatim - what is wrong is whose result the corpus says it is. Nothing edited, nothing withdrawn: the row is marked so a page can name the source. Where the record is a commentary or review, its `claim_relations` layer usually already names the paper being discussed - the record knows at one layer and forgets at another.
span.quote: Importantly, the authors 18 observed that cells firing later in the delay period were active for longer durations (that is, they had larger ‘time-fields’) ( FIG. 1 ), a phenomenon that was also observed in other studies 19 , 20 (discussed below). This pattern suggests a scalar coding of time, which parallels a hallmark property of time judgements in humans and animals, as discussed below.

span.label: THE IDENTITY CLAIM: time cells are the same neurons as place cells, and in freely moving animals fire only when the animal is in a particular location
span.quote: Time cells are the same neurons as place cells. One line of evidence supporting this conclusion is that, in freely moving animals, time cells are activated only when the animal is in a particular location

span.label: the same cells that fired at particular moments on the treadmill fired at particular places on the maze outside it
span.quote: Indeed, some of the same neurons that fired at particular moments in time (that is, time cells) on the treadmill also fired when the rat passed through specific locations on the maze outside the treadmill, showing that these cells also function as place cells

span.label: the reorganisation of time cells when a temporal cue changes parallels the reorganisation of place cells when spatial cues change
span.quote: Thus, the partial reorganization of firing patterns of time cells that occurs when a critical temporal cue is altered closely parallels the partial reorganization of place cells that occurs when spatial cues are altered.

span.label: temporal cues and structure control time cells just as spatial cues and structure control place cells
span.quote: Time cells are controlled by the temporal cues (the beginning and end of an episode) and the temporal structure (critical intervals) of an experience, just as place cells are controlled by the spatial cues (landmarks) and the spatial structure (shape) of the environment.

span.label: the proposal that follows is to treat hippocampal principal neurons as multidimensional rather than as either kind of cell
span.quote: Thus, it may be more productive to think of hippocampal principal neurons as multidimensional, in the sense that they encode time and place along with other relevant spatial and non-spatial features of ongoing experience

span.label: temporal coding is tied to memory three ways: it develops with learning, it is memory-specific, and it predicts judgement accuracy
span.quote: Temporal coding has been linked to memory performance in three ways: first, temporal coding develops as animals acquire temporally structured memories; second, distinct temporal codes are associated with specific memories; and third, temporal coding predicts accurate memory judgements about individual events.

span.label: A DOUBLE GRADIENT IN MONKEYS: time coding falls and object-identity coding rises going from entorhinal to perirhinal to inferotemporal cortex
span.quote: The proportion of cells encoding time decreased from entorhinal cortex to perirhinal cortex to infero-temporal cortex (upstream of the hippocampus), whereas the proportion of cells encoding object identity increased.

span.label: QUALIFICATION ON THE CROSS-SPECIES CLAIM: the human patterns are slowly changing rather than punctate, closer to an earlier rat result than to the rodent time cells
span.quote: Although these slowly changing activity patterns more closely resemble the gradually evolving time signal in the study by Manns et al. 12 than the sequences of punctate time-cell activations in the above-described studies on rodents, these observations clearly demonstrate that temporal coding by neuronal activity related to memory also occurs in the human hippocampus.

span.label: place-cell sequences replay in compressed form during sleep and quiet wakefulness, so spatial coding is recapitulated temporally
span.quote: many studies have reported that ensembles of simultaneously recorded place cells that fire in sequential locations as animals traverse a path through a maze subsequently ‘replay’ the corresponding sequence of firings during ‘off-line’ periods, including sleep and quiet wakefulness, when the animal is not moving through those locations

span.label: when spatial and sequence strategies compete, the firing sequences follow whichever strategy the animal expressed on that probe trial
span.quote: Analysis of neural activity revealed that firing sequences of hippocampal neurons reflected the strategy expressed on these probe trials — that is, when the mice ran towards the learned location, which required a new sequence of body turns, the neurons fired at consistent locations in the maze.

span.label: FOUR ARGUMENTS AGAINST STRICT CHAINING, first: the cells changed their firing patterns even during the initial part of the delay, rather than simply adding cell activations during the extended segment
span.quote: That is, the cells changed their temporal firing patterns even during the initial part of the delay (thus creating a new temporal context representation), rather than simply adding cell activations during the extended segment of the delay

span.label: second: strict chains cannot split to encode overlapping memories that share identical events
span.quote: Strict firing chains cannot ‘split’ to differently encode overlapping memories, although different initial elements in a sequence could specify a distinct sequence of succeeding elements that represent overlapping events

span.label: third: scalar firing is inconsistent with uniform-duration chain activations and consistent with the scalar temporal context model
span.quote: In addition, firing sequences of time cells are usually scalar, so that time cells that fire later in a sequence also fire for a longer period ( FIGS 1b , 2B ; but see REF. 16 ). This is inconsistent with firing chains involving uniform-duration neuronal activations but is consistent with a recent variation on the temporal context model known as the scalar temporal context model

span.label: fourth: compressed replay would need a mechanism that can decompress back to the original intervals
span.quote: Although it is easy to imagine the compression of firing chains by simply having fewer spikes per cell and the subsequent decompression as longer spike bursts, a reproduction of an externally generated representation of real-time context representations would require a more complex compression mechanism that allows decompression to reconstruct the original intervals.

span.label: on the other side, firing chains appear to be preconfigured and then co-opted to organise events
span.quote: These findings suggest that firing chains are preconfigured within the hippocampus and are then co-opted to provide temporal organizations of events.

span.quote: Combining the findings that support the existence of firing chains with the observations that a broader signal that defines entire memories is needed, perhaps the most likely network mechanism involves slowly evolving temporal context dynamics (that is, signals that spread across multiple sequential events) selecting specific firing chains that represent specific temporally organized memories

span.quote: there is recent evidence that medial entorhinal cortex neurons that fire when a rat is in particular locations in space (known as ‘grid cells’) also fire at particular moments during treadmill running

span.label: judging intervals and remembering temporal organisation are separated, with the hippocampus secondary to the first and central to the second
span.quote: This view is consistent with a recently proposed distinction between the ability to judge temporal intervals, in which the hippocampus has a secondary role, and memory for temporal organization, in which the hippocampus is central

span.label: the review's headline consequence: this challenges spatial mapping and navigation as the fundamental function of the hippocampus
span.quote: This challenges the view that the fundamental function of the hippocampus is spatial mapping and navigation 75 , and instead supports the notion that the hippocampus contributes to memory by organizing elements of experience in both spatial and temporal context.

span.label: THE AUTHOR'S CLOSING DEFLATION: it remains entirely possible that both dimensions reduce to association by proximity, making time cells and place cells reflections of one associative function
span.quote: Finally, although both spatial and temporal coding are prevalent in the activity patterns of hippocampal neurons, and can be distinguished experimentally, it remains entirely possible that the common thread in both dimensions is ‘association by proximity’ in space or time. This would suggest that place cells and time cells are simply reflections of a basic function of the hippocampus — supporting associative networks that represent a broad range of relations among the elements of memories

span.label: over 80% — neurons active during treadmill running whose activity was modulated by elapsed time
span.quote: A general linear model analysis that considered head position, time and distance revealed that the activity of over 80% of the neurons that were active during treadmill running was modulated by elapsed time. Position had little influence, but distance travelled was also strongly encoded in the activity of many neurons. The firing patterns of some neurons signalled only time or only distance, but the activity of most cells was influenced to differing degrees by both variables, indicating that most of these cells encoded both time and distance.
